title: Choose a supported Linux distribution for Hyper-V
author: Marcos Nogueira
description: Selecting a supported Linux distribution for Hyper-V requires checking LIS integration, kernel version, and secure boot compatibility.

sources.title: Supported Linux and FreeBSD virtual machines for Hyper-V on Windows Server and Windows
Supported Ubuntu virtual machines on Hyper-V
CentOS and Red Hat Enterprise Linux VMs on Hyper-V

open_questions: Does the user need to know about specific kernel version requirements for older distributions?
Are there any known issues with SR-IOV on specific Linux versions that should be mentioned?
Should the article include more details on how to verify LIS installation inside the guest OS?
review_status: Bulk draft; automated structural checks only. Detailed source, code and visual review remains pending.

bulk_preparation.previous_editor_findings: Prior model feedback retained; not independently confirmed resolved

claim_support_checks.claim: Emulated devices do not provide high performance or full management infrastructure.
Built-in LIS drivers are included in modern distributions and should not be replaced by Microsoft downloads.
Installing separate LIS on RHEL may limit Red Hat support.
Secure boot is enabled by default on Generation 2 VMs and may prevent Linux boot.
Dynamic memory parameters must be in multiples of 128 MB.

model_editor_issues.problem: The draft includes a duplicate 'Further documentation' paragraph at the very end, violating editing standards for clean output.
model_editor_issues.fix: Remove the second block of 'Further documentation' links. Keep only the first instance to avoid redundancy and improve readability.

model_editor_issues.problem: The Ubuntu VHD copy workaround (renaming shimx64.efi) is presented as a general step for 'Ubuntu Generation 2 VMs' but is a specific fix for certain image configurations, not a universal requirement.
model_editor_issues.fix: Clarify that this is a specific workaround for boot path issues in cloned images, not a standard setup step for all Ubuntu Gen 2 VMs. Ensure it is clearly marked as an exception handling procedure.

model_editor_issues.problem: The draft claims 'Built-in LIS drivers are included in modern distributions' without defining 'modern'. It also implies RHEL/CentOS 8/9 are the only ones with built-in LIS, ignoring other supported distros like Debian/SUSE listed in S1.
model_editor_issues.fix: Specify that RHEL/CentOS 8+ and Ubuntu 16.04+ have built-in LIS. Avoid vague terms like 'modern' and ensure the scope reflects all supported distros mentioned in the source index (S1).

model_editor_issues.problem: The draft states 'Dynamic memory... requires careful configuration' but does not mention the 64-bit requirement explicitly in the main text, only in the notes.
model_editor_issues.fix: Move the '64-bit virtual machines only' constraint to the primary bullet point or introductory sentence of the Dynamic Memory section for immediate visibility.
